title_or_artifact: Estimation of three-dimensional ground reaction forces using low-cost smart insoles
locator: Zhang D.; Liu Y.; Exell T.; Huang Y.; Zhou D.; Guo L. Intelligent Sports and Health 1(1):40–50 (2025). DOI:10.1016/j.ish.2024.12.005; full-text PDF accessed via https://www.newswise.com/pdf_docs/174014701229478_1-s2.0-S3050544525000027-main.pdf
verified_scope: Abstract and main text read: CapSense+IMU dual-stream attention estimates 3D-GRF; synchronized force plates used as reference; reported lowest NRMSE 4.1% in the stated protocol.
limitations_or_next_action: Different sensor stack (CapSense+IMU, not Velostat); not evidence of longitudinal drift robustness or biology-vs-sensor separation.

title_or_artifact: Development of a Self-Powered Piezo-Resistive Smart Insole Equipped with Low-Power BLE Connectivity for Remote Gait Monitoring
locator: de Fazio R.; Perrone E.; Velázquez R.; De Vittorio M.; Visconti P. Sensors 21(13):4539 (2021). DOI:10.3390/s21134539; https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/21/13/4539
verified_scope: Article page read in part: a Velostat piezoresistive matrix was characterized for load/repeatability/hysteresis and its firmware used a history/time-dependent corrective term for a transient effect.
limitations_or_next_action: Not a force-plate-validated 3D-GRF study and not evidence that correction separates biological change from sensor/environment change across sessions.

title_or_artifact: Simple, Commercially Viable Insole Sensor for Simultaneous Plantar Pressure and Shear Stress Measurement Using Tilted Piezoresistive Sensors

verified_scope: Abstract and characterization section read: five oriented piezoresistive sensors/module infer normal and shear stress; article reports notable initial drift and stabilization behavior in a sensor under cyclic testing.
limitations_or_next_action: Different sensor/module and treadmill context; no demonstrated long-term biological-versus-sensor decomposition.

title_or_artifact: Wireless pressure insoles for measuring ground reaction forces and trajectories of the centre of pressure during functional activities
locator: Scientific Reports (2023). DOI:10.1038/s41598-023-41622-3; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-41622-3
verified_scope: Abstract and methods read: two same-day sessions, force-plate comparison and test-retest assessment; AP COP trajectories were comparable, whereas ML trajectories and vGRF differed systematically from force plates.
limitations_or_next_action: Same-day test-retest is not 30-day cross-session drift correction; pressure insole does not establish Fx/Fy validation.

title_or_artifact: Wearable-sensor based walking and non-walking measures as progression markers in early to mid-stage Parkinson’s disease
locator: npj Parkinson's Disease (2026). DOI:10.1038/s41531-026-01358-z; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-026-01358-z
verified_scope: Abstract and methods introduction read: longitudinal wrist wearable measures were evaluated for reliability, sensitivity to within-participant change, and comparison with non-PD participants; changes were detectable from 10 months in the stated cohort.
limitations_or_next_action: Different disease, body location, and sensor; supports feasibility principles only, not knee-OA claims or insole kinetic validity.

title_or_artifact: The individuality of plantar pressure indices enables the reduction of descriptive gait data required for diagnostic purposes
locator: Scientific Reports (2025). DOI:10.1038/s41598-025-16428-0; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-16428-0
verified_scope: Abstract and introduction read: study quantified intra- versus inter-individual plantar-pressure variation in 19 healthy young women across 200 walking trials and discusses subsequent-session changes.
limitations_or_next_action: Pressure-platform study in a narrow healthy cohort; it does not decompose sensor drift and should not be generalized to OA.

title_or_artifact: Reliable Vertical Ground Reaction Force Estimation with Smart Insole During Walking
locator: Olugbon F.; Ghoreishi N.; Huang M.-C.; Xu W.; Chen D. arXiv:2501.07748 (2025). DOI:10.48550/arXiv.2501.07748; https://arxiv.org/html/2501.07748v1
verified_scope: Preprint main text read: identifies pressure-sensor drift and poor generalization as limitations; uses IMU plus center of pressed sensors (binary pressure-switch treatment) with ANN/RF/LSTM for vGRF; reports intra-/inter-participant performance.
limitations_or_next_action: Preprint, not peer reviewed; vGRF only; read scope did not establish a multi-day/session study, a 3D-GRF/COP result, or biology-versus-sensor attribution.

title_or_artifact: Evaluation of the Foot Center of Pressure Estimation from Pressure Insoles during Sidestep Cuts, Runs and Walks
locator: Blin J.; et al. Sensors 22(15):5628 (2022). PMID:35957186. DOI:10.3390/s22155628; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35957186/
verified_scope: Abstract read: best CoP accuracy occurred when calibration motion matched the evaluated motion; accuracy also increased with vertical force and the number of involved pressure cells.
limitations_or_next_action: Does not establish a longitudinal sensor-state model; need full-method review before specifying all confounds or generalizing to project hardware.

title_or_artifact: Center of Pressure Measurement Accuracy via Insoles with a Reduced Pressure Sensor Number during Gaits
locator: Fuchs P.X.; Chen W.-H.; Shiang T.-Y. Sensors 24(15):4918 (2024). DOI:10.3390/s24154918; PMCID:PMC11315048; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11315048/
verified_scope: Abstract and article metadata read: 12 participants, 99-sensor reference insole and simulated 3–17-sensor layouts across walking/jogging/running; concordance and RMSE vary by layout and gait.

title_or_artifact: Benchmarking study of the forces and centre of pressure derived from a novel smart-insole against an existing pressure measuring insole and force plate
locator: Weizman Y.; Tan A.M.; Fuss F.K. Measurement 142:48–59 (2019). DOI:10.1016/j.measurement.2019.03.023; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0263224119302325
verified_scope: Abstract/preview read: benchmarked smart insole and Pedar against Kistler force plate; states that stacking/relative position of one insole to another affected accuracy and that in-shoe systems cannot measure horizontal GRF directly.

title_or_artifact: A Low-Cost Instrumented Shoe System for Gait Phase Detection Based on Foot Plantar Pressure Data
locator: Hu X.; Duan Q.; Tang J.; Chen G.; Zhao Z.; Sun Z.; Chen C.; Qu X. IEEE Journal of Translational Engineering in Health and Medicine 12:84–96. DOI:10.1109/JTEHM.2023.3319576; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10712682/
verified_scope: Abstract and methods/discussion read: 174-cell Velostat matrix; zero-potential crosstalk method; gait-phase detection for straight and turning walking; multiple-cell regional aggregation used because cells change at different rates.
limitations_or_next_action: Gait-phase target, not force-plate 3D-GRF/COP or longitudinal measurement-integrity validation; 174 cells exceeds current direct 16-ADC assumption.

title_or_artifact: Validity and reliability of the XSENSOR in-shoe pressure measurement system

title_or_artifact: Repeatability of Vertical Ground Reaction Force Estimation During Running on the Athletics Track on 3 Different Days

title_or_artifact: Test-retest reliability and usability evaluation of a wearable plantar pressure monitoring system for linear and curved walking

title_or_artifact: Prediction of Three-Directional Ground Reaction Forces during Walking Using a Shoe Sole Sensor System and Machine Learning

title_or_artifact: Effect of pressure insole sampling frequency on insole-measured peak force accuracy during running
locator: Elstub L.J.; Grohowski L.M.; Wolf D.N.; Owen M.K.; Noehren B.; Zelik K.E. Journal of Biomechanics 145:111387 (2022). DOI:10.1016/j.jbiomech.2022.111387; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0021929022004286
verified_scope: Abstract and introduction read: downsampled 100-Hz Pedar data shows a sampling-rate/battery/peak-force-error trade-off; peak force error remained below 3% down to 20 Hz in the studied running conditions.
limitations_or_next_action: Post-hoc downsampling of one commercial system in running; does not validate multiplexed Velostat temporal behavior, COP, 3D-GRF, or longitudinal sensor-state attribution.

title_or_artifact: Consumer-priced wearable sensors combined with deep learning can be used to accurately predict ground reaction forces during various treadmill running conditions
locator: Carter J.; Chen X.; Cazzola D.; Trewartha G.; Preatoni E. PeerJ 12:e17896 (2024). DOI:10.7717/peerj.17896; PMCID:PMC11366233; https://peerj.com/articles/17896/
verified_scope: Abstract/methods read: 50 runners; pressure insole of 16 resistive FSR channels + IMU; LSTM estimates vertical and anteroposterior GRF traces with leave-one-subject-out validation across speeds/gradients; mean rRMSE 3.2% (GRFv) and 3.1% (GRFap).
limitations_or_next_action: Generalization across subjects/conditions, not longitudinal sessions; no explicit measurement-integrity state, no false biological-change alert endpoint, no abstention/coverage. Does not kill the candidate.

title_or_artifact: In-shoe plantar shear stress sensor design, calibration and evaluation for the diabetic foot
locator: Haron A.H.; Li L.; Shuang J.; Lin C.; Dawes H.; Mansoubi M.; et al. PLOS ONE 19(9):e0309514 (2024). DOI:10.1371/journal.pone.0309514; https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0309514
verified_scope: Abstract read: strain-gauge shear array in silicone insole + normal-pressure backing; custom rig varied indenter area (78.5-707 mm2) and position (up to 40 mm off-centre); calibration-factor variation up to 80% (area) and 90% (position); bench repeatability >97%, MAE <18 kPa; <21% variability within 15-min walking.
limitations_or_next_action: Strong controlled-calibration-perturbation evidence (area/location dominate readings) but it is a calibration/feasibility study; no integrity-state estimator, no longitudinal-change decision, no false-alert or abstention endpoint. Does not kill the candidate.

title_or_artifact: Testing protocols and measurement techniques when using pressure sensors for sport and health applications: A comparative review
locator: Burnie L.; Chockalingam N.; Holder A.; Claypole T.; Kilduff L.; Bezodis N. Foot (Edinb) 59:102094 (2024). DOI:10.1016/j.foot.2024.102094; PMID:38579518
verified_scope: Abstract/highlights read: comparative review of platform vs in-shoe systems, testing protocols, calibration suitability, and AI potential; notes calibration loading rates are often lower than real gait and application-specific calibration is needed.
limitations_or_next_action: Review-level map of calibration/protocol limitations; not an integrity estimator, no longitudinal alert or abstention endpoint. Matrix previously mis-attributed this to J Biomech; correct venue is Foot (Edinb). Does not kill the candidate.

title_or_artifact: Device-dependent variability of plantar pressure thresholds: Consequences for clinical decision-making in diabetic foot care
locator: Chockalingam N.; Healy A.C.; Sacco I.C.N.; et al. Gait and Posture 126:110128 (2026). DOI:10.1016/j.gaitpost.2026.110128; PMID:41690051; PII:S0966636226000366
verified_scope: Abstract + discussion read: 15 healthy adults, 3 platform + 2 in-shoe systems; fixed 200/600 kPa thresholds; cross-device classification agreement for 600 kPa only 5.4% (heel 7.1%, forefoot 3.6%); rearfoot-forefoot ratio 53.6% and most-loaded-region 6.7% agreement; concludes absolute thresholds are unreliable and recommends device-specific/within-patient/multidimensional approaches.
limitations_or_next_action: Strong evidence that measurement-system state changes clinical classification (misclassification risk) but proposes guideline change, NOT an operational integrity estimator, longitudinal false-alert endpoint, or abstention/coverage. Closest clinical-decision neighbour; does not kill the candidate.

title_or_artifact: A wireless, self-powered smart insole for gait monitoring and recognition via nonlinear synergistic pressure sensing
locator: Wang Q.; Guan H.; Wang C.; et al. Science Advances 11:eadu1598 (2025). DOI:10.1126/sciadv.adu1598; https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.adu1598
verified_scope: Abstract/summary read: 22 CNT/ACET/PDMS sensors + perovskite solar harvesting; nonlinear synergistic strategy, R2>0.999 over 0-225 kPa; >180,000 compression-cycle durability; SVM classifies 8 motion states; 32 Hz sampling.
limitations_or_next_action: Sensor durability/cycle-life and activity-recognition result; 180k cycles is a materials endurance metric, not longitudinal biological-change validity; no integrity state, false-alert, or abstention endpoint. Does not kill the candidate.

title_or_artifact: Sensor Insoles: A Review
locator: Latsch B.; Herbst F.; Suppelt M.; Seiler J.; Schaumann S.; Suppelt S.; Altmann A.A.; Grimmer M.; Kupnik M. IEEE Sensors Journal 26(3):3577-3596 (2026). DOI:10.1109/JSEN.2025.3638124; arXiv:2509.00260
verified_scope: Abstract + selected excerpts read: reviews >40 insoles across modalities; identifies lack of proper calibration, gait-based verification, and human validation; proposes testing-machine + instrumented-treadmill gold standard; only 9 of 41 works use a reference for both sensor testing and gait; frames 'measurement disturbance' (human foot mechanically perturbs the calibrated sensor) with tissue stiffness as a key uncertainty source.
limitations_or_next_action: Peer-reviewed review that MOTIVATES the gap (calibration/verification discipline, measurement disturbance) but does not build an operational integrity estimator or a longitudinal false-alert/abstention system. Supports, does not kill, the candidate.

title_or_artifact: Monitoring Mobility at Home: The GAIT-HUB Sensor-Based Protocol for Remote Gait Analysis
locator: Pilloni G.; Ko T.S.H.; Kreisberg E.; Geel J.; Gutman J.M.; Sammarco C.; Oh C.; Charvet L. Digital Biomarkers 9(1):140-154 (2025). DOI:10.1159/000547176; PMCID:PMC12310191; PMID:40740790
verified_scope: Abstract read: 29 MS participants; in-clinic G-Sensor baseline + 3 weekly remotely-supervised home sessions with RunScribe shoe sensors; ICC and Bland-Altman cross-device agreement; longitudinal reliability of remote assessments + SUS usability.
limitations_or_next_action: Home longitudinal reliability/placement-supervision protocol with cross-device agreement, but no explicit measurement-integrity state, no false biological-change alert endpoint, and no abstention/coverage. Does not kill the candidate.

title_or_artifact: Real-World Gait Detection Using a Wrist-Worn Inertial Sensor: Validation Study
locator: Kluge F.; Brand Y.E.; Mico-Amigo M.E.; Bertuletti S.; et al. JMIR Formative Research 8:e50035 (2024). DOI:10.2196/50035; PMCID:PMC11097052
verified_scope: Identity + author list verified from PMC article page; wrist-worn IMU validation of real-world gait-event detection with explicit TP/FP/FN and specificity trade-offs.
limitations_or_next_action: Wrist IMU gait-event detection, not plantar pressure; decision-metric logic (TP/FP/FN, specificity) is transferable but device/task differ; no measurement-integrity protocol. Does not kill the candidate.

title_or_artifact: Sensor Health Monitoring reduces false-positive alerts from unhealthy sensor data (industrial asset-performance monitoring)
locator: GE Vernova APM SmartSignal vendor documentation/blog, 'How Sensor Health Monitoring Helps You Gain Confidence in Your Data & Alerts'; https://www.gevernova.com/software/blog/how-sensor-health-monitoring-helps-you-gain-confidence-your-data-alerts
verified_scope: Vendor page read: describes scoring sensor health, suppressing alerts driven by unhealthy data, and reconfiguring the digital twin to 'further reduce false-positive alerts', with historical records of sensor-health activity and recovery.
limitations_or_next_action: NON-ACADEMIC vendor/marketing source, not a peer-reviewed study. Establishes that the general engineering pattern 'monitor sensor integrity -> suppress data-driven false alerts' is already deployed in rotating-machinery APM (via analytic redundancy/residuals, not injected perturbations). Constrains novelty framing; not plantar sensing, not longitudinal biological change, not perturbation-injection.

title_or_artifact: Sensing Techniques for Structural Health Monitoring: A State-of-the-Art Review on Performance Criteria and New-Generation Technologies
locator: PMC11902730 (2025); https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11902730/
verified_scope: Selected excerpt read: states that quantifying operational and environmental conditions enables data normalization, 'preventing benign changes from being misinterpreted as damage and thereby reducing the risk of false alarms (Type I errors)'.
limitations_or_next_action: Structural (not plantar/gait) domain; establishes that 'normalize for operational/environmental state so benign changes are not misread as damage' is an established performance criterion. Author list not captured. Analogous pattern in a different field; does not kill the candidate.

title_or_artifact: Lumbar Acceleration Gait Estimation: 'Step-by-Step' Algorithm Updates and Improvements
locator: Journal of Medical Internet Research 27(1):e72831 (2025); https://www.jmir.org/2025/1/e72831

limitations_or_next_action: IMU gait-estimation algorithm paper; frames the biology-vs-algorithm attribution concern for longitudinal monitoring but does not implement a measurement-integrity estimator, perturbation library, or coverage/abstention endpoint. Supports the problem framing; does not kill the candidate.
